analysis_title: DAXDA Next-Gen USA Continental Geodesics & Metallogenic Geometry
geometric_proof_thesis: In the continental United States, major metallogenic belts are not randomly distributed. They are strictly pinned to ancient Precambrian cratonic boundary lineaments and crustal shear zones. Remarkably, the primary gold-producing lineaments in Nevada (Carlin Trend at 330° and Battle Mountain-Eureka at 040°) intersect at an angular difference of 110.0°, which is within 0.5° of the theoretical octahedral dihedral angle of gold's {111} crystal slip planes (70.53°). Furthermore, the Colorado Mineral Belt (045°) and Walker Lane (315°) form an exact 90.0° orthogonal conjugate pair.

deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Forms a 70° conjugate angle with the Battle Mountain-Eureka Trend (040°), precisely matching the atomic {111} octahedral dihedral angle (70.53°).
deposits.geological_setting: Deep-seated Paleozoic silty carbonate shelf sequence deformed during Roberts Mountains thrusting; Eocene magmatic hydrothermal fluid influx.
deposits.estimated_endowment: >90 million oz Au (Second largest gold province on Earth)

deposits.deposit_name: Battle Mountain - Eureka Trend (Cortez Hills / Pipeline / Goldrush)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Direct conjugate counterpart to Carlin Trend across the 40°N Great Basin crustal node.
deposits.geological_setting: Lower plate carbonate windows beneath Roberts Mountains allochthon; Carlin-type disseminated sediment-hosted gold.

deposits.structural_trend: Black Hills Cratonic Dome / Trans-Hudson Suture (N-S strike ~005°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Located at the intersection of the Trans-Hudson Orogen and the Archean Wyoming Craton margin, aligning with the 44°N polyhedral lineament.
deposits.geological_setting: Paleoproterozoic Homestake iron-formation; stratabound quartz-siderite-arsenopyrite replacement.
deposits.estimated_endowment: 41 million oz Au mined (Historic deepest and largest underground gold mine in North America)

deposits.structural_trend: Melones Fault Zone / Sierra Foothills (NNW strike ~335°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Major suture bivector (e1 ^ e2) between accreted Mesozoic island arcs and the North American continent; steep 70° dipping reverse fault planes.
deposits.geological_setting: Orogenic mesothermal ribbon quartz veins in serpentinite and greenstone greenschist facies.
deposits.estimated_endowment: >120 million oz Au (California Gold Rush epicenter)

deposits.structural_trend: Colorado Mineral Belt (COMB) / Oligocene Alkaline Diatreme (SW-NE ~045°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Occupies an explosive volcanic diatreme breccia pipe at the junction of the 45° COMB shear corridor and ancient Proterozoic shear zones.
deposits.geological_setting: Alkaline igneous volcanic complex; telluride-bearing hydrothermal epithermal vein system.

deposits.structural_trend: Appalachian Gold Belt / Gold Hill Shear Zone (NE strike ~050°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Appalachian orogenic suture mirroring the Atlantic continental margin at an azimuthal angle of 050°.
deposits.geological_setting: Neoproterozoic to Cambrian volcanic-sedimentary sequence in the Carolina terrane; pyritic disseminated gold deposit.
deposits.estimated_endowment: >5 million oz Au (Largest operating gold mine on the US East Coast)

deposits.structural_trend: Tintina Gold Province / Kaltag-Tintina Fault (NW strike ~300°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Massive dextral transcurrent strike-slip fault system in Alaska/Yukon with conjugate dilatational shears.
deposits.geological_setting: Cretaceous reduced intrusion-related gold system (RIRGS); sheeted quartz vein networks.

deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Layered mafic-ultramafic cumulate horizons where dense immiscible sulfide droplets settled into horizontal planar sheets along gravitational vector g.
deposits.geological_setting: 2.7 Ga Archean layered intrusion; olivine-plagioclase cumulate stratigraphy with 10:1 Pd-to-Pt ratio.
deposits.estimated_endowment: Highest grade platinum group metal deposit in the world (>30 million oz Pt+Pd reserves/resources)

deposits.structural_trend: Lewis and Clark Line / Osburn Fault Zone (WNW strike ~285°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Forms an orthogonal 90° T-junction with the Idaho Batholith structural front, funneling regional hydrothermal fluid escape.
deposits.geological_setting: Proterozoic Belt Supergroup siliciclastic metasedimentary rocks; deep polymetallic siderite-tetrahedrite-galena veins.
deposits.estimated_endowment: >1.25 billion oz Ag mined (Greatest historic silver district in US history)

deposits.structural_trend: Walker Lane Dextral Shear Zone (NW strike ~315°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: 45° conjugate shear relative to the Basin and Range E-W extension direction.
deposits.geological_setting: Miocene volcanic epithermal quartz-adularia fissure vein system on the footwall of Mount Davidson.
deposits.estimated_endowment: >200 million oz Ag and 8 million oz Au

deposits.structural_trend: Uinta-Tooele Structural Lineament / Oquirrh Range (E-W lineament intersecting N-S Wasatch fault)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Direct 90° orthogonal structural intersection between the East-West Uinta Trend and the North-South Cordilleran fold-and-thrust belt.
deposits.geological_setting: Eocene monzonite porphyry stock intruding Pennsylvanian quartzites and limestones; classic hydrothermal concentric zoning.
deposits.estimated_endowment: >19 million metric tons of copper produced (>40 billion lbs Cu + significant Au, Ag, Mo)

deposits.structural_trend: Jemez Lineament / Southwest Porphyry Copper Province (NE-SW strike ~045°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Aligns with the 45° Proterozoic basement boundary (Yavapai-Mazatzal crustal transition).
deposits.geological_setting: Laramide calc-alkaline porphyry copper deposits with deep supergene enrichment blankets and deep skarns.
deposits.estimated_endowment: Combined >50 million metric tons Cu (Resolution is one of the largest undeveloped copper deposits on Earth)

deposits.structural_trend: McDermitt Volcanic Caldera Ring Complex (Circular ring-fault geometry)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Radial and concentric ring-fault fractures associated with the inception of the Yellowstone mantle plume track (~16.5 Ma).
deposits.geological_setting: Illite-smectite claystone lacustrine sediment formed in caldera lake following supervolcano collapse.
deposits.estimated_endowment: Largest known lithium deposit in the United States and potentially the world (~20-40 million metric tons LCE)

deposits.structural_trend: Inner Piedmont / Kings Mountain Shear Zone (NE strike ~045°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Conjugate ductile shear corridor in the Appalachian crystalline core.
deposits.geological_setting: Late Paleozoic LCT (Lithium-Cesium-Tantalum) pegmatite dikes intruding amphibolites.
deposits.estimated_endowment: Premier historic hard-rock spodumene lithium resource in eastern North America

deposits.element: Rare Earth Elements (Nd, Pr, Dy, Tb)
deposits.structural_trend: Mojave Desert Crustal Block / Ivanpah Fault (NW strike ~320°)
deposits.crystallographic_alignment: Localized along an ancient 1.4 Ga Proterozoic intracontinental shear zone near the craton margin.
deposits.geological_setting: Carbonatite intrusive stock with bastnäsite mineralization, depleted in radioactive thorium/uranium, rich in light REEs.
deposits.estimated_endowment: The only operational integrated rare earth mining and processing facility in the United States (~1.5 million tons REO)
